newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee likely to consolidate, support holds.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee likely to consolidate, support holds.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

LIFFE coffee futures, consolidating their recent gains, are likely to hold near-term support at $2,050 basis July but could struggle to take out the immediate $2,145 resistance, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
Traders called the market to open $20-$25 down.
Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst, said coffee was looking very toppy.
The 14-day relative strength indicator (RSI) was well in the overbought zone of 81 percent.
But Gifford said the market could find an immediate floor at $2,050, followed by $2,030, the low on May 21.
On the upside, she pegged resistance levels at $2,145, and then the May 19 peak of $2,190, the highest level since January 31, 1996.
"I doubt the $2,145 level will be taken out. The market will continue to consolidate," she added.
Last week's rally was fuelled by news that the Association of Coffee Producing Countries agreed to extend their export curbs for one more year from July 1.
Traders said the market's immediate concern now was the Brazilian weather as the country's coffee areas entered the critical frost danger period in June and July.
No damaging cold was expected for this week in Brazil's coffee belt, U.S. private forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday.
It said conditions for the trees and the maturing crop were generally favourable at this time.
The last major frosts in 1994, one in June and another in July, damaged many of Brazil's trees and sent world prices spiralling.
